claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of eight self-controlled case series studies across six countries found no significant increase in stroke risk after Pfizer-BioNTech (BNT162b2) COVID-19 vaccination, with a pooled incidence rate ratio of 0.967 (95% CI 0.892-1.049).
label: True

claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of eight self-controlled case series studies across six countries found that Pfizer-BioNTech (BNT162b2) COVID-19 vaccination cut stroke risk by more than half, with a pooled incidence rate ratio of 0.45 (95% CI 0.38-0.53).
label: False

claim: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies found that vaccinating pregnant women against RSV cut infant RSV-related hospitalisations by about 80% within 3 months of birth and about 68% through 6 months, with no robustly significant increase in preterm birth for the licensed Pfizer vaccine.
label: True

claim: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies found that vaccinating pregnant women against RSV cut infant RSV-related hospitalisations by only about 8% within 3 months of birth and had no measurable effect through 6 months, while the licensed Pfizer vaccine more than doubled the risk of preterm birth.
label: False

claim: A scoping review of 13 studies published from 2014 to 2024 found that clear aligner therapy contributes to plastic waste, microplastic generation and greenhouse gas emissions throughout its life cycle, and that fixes like biodegradable materials, direct 3D printing and recycling remain constrained by limited infrastructure, cost and insufficient high-quality evidence.
label: True

claim: A scoping review of 13 studies published from 2014 to 2024 found that clear aligner therapy generates virtually no plastic waste, microplastics or greenhouse gas emissions throughout its life cycle, and that fixes like biodegradable materials, direct 3D printing and recycling are already widely implemented, backed by robust high-quality evidence.
label: False

claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of 4 studies covering 8,769 adults found that eating more ultra-processed food was not significantly linked to infertility risk (RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.94-1.69), though the estimate leaned toward higher risk.
label: True

claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of 4 studies covering 8,769 adults found that eating more ultra-processed food significantly raised infertility risk, with risk more than tripling (RR 3.26, 95% CI 2.94-3.69).
label: False

claim: A recent systematic review and meta-analysis of 46 studies found that higher ultra-processed food consumption was associated with a 9% higher risk of cardiovascular disease and a 16% higher risk of hypertension.
label: True

claim: A recent systematic review and meta-analysis of 46 studies found that higher ultra-processed food consumption was associated with a 9% lower risk of cardiovascular disease and a 16% lower risk of hypertension.
label: False

claim: A meta-analysis of 5 randomized trials and 120 healthy adults, with literature searched through November 2023, found that time-restricted feeding combined with resistance training did not significantly change fat-free mass compared with a conventional diet (-0.48 kg, 95% CI -2.52 to 1.56).
label: True

claim: A meta-analysis of 5 randomized trials and 120 healthy adults, with literature searched through November 2023, found that time-restricted feeding combined with resistance training significantly increased fat-free mass compared with a conventional diet, adding an average of 2.5 kg of lean mass (95% CI 1.56 to 3.44).
label: False

claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of 36 studies on type 2 diabetes remission found that BMI cuts both ways: higher BMI was linked to higher odds of remission after surgery (OR 1.05) but lower odds with non-surgical interventions (OR 0.89).
label: True

claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of 36 studies on type 2 diabetes remission found that BMI cuts both ways: higher BMI was linked to lower odds of remission after surgery (OR 0.89) but higher odds with non-surgical interventions (OR 1.05).
label: False

claim: A systematic review of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction guidelines, searched through November 2024, found that 7 of 12 met rigour criteria. They broadly agreed on diagnosis and core drug therapies, but differed on natriuretic peptide thresholds and device therapies, and only a minority addressed comorbidities like iron deficiency and frailty.
label: True

claim: A systematic review of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction guidelines, searched through November 2024, found that all 12 met rigour criteria. They fully agreed on diagnosis, core drug therapies, natriuretic peptide thresholds and device therapies, and nearly all addressed comorbidities like iron deficiency and frailty.
label: False

claim: A reanalysis of a 2024 meta-analysis, limited to 8 low-risk-of-bias randomized trials with 30,320 participants, found vitamin D supplementation lowered all-cause mortality by 4% (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.92–1.00), an evidence signal for people aged 75+ that still needs confirmation.
label: True

claim: A reanalysis of a 2024 meta-analysis, limited to 8 low-risk-of-bias randomized trials with 30,320 participants, found vitamin D supplementation raised all-cause mortality by 4% (RR 1.04, 95% CI 1.00–1.08), a harm signal for people aged 75+ that still needs confirmation.
label: False

claim: A meta-analysis of 45 randomized controlled trials found that oral vitamin D supplements modestly improved cardiometabolic risk factors compared with placebo in adults, lowering LDL cholesterol by 0.136 mmol/L, systolic blood pressure by 2.79 mm Hg, fasting blood glucose by 0.11 mmol/L and HbA1c by 0.164%.
label: True

claim: A meta-analysis of 45 randomized controlled trials found that oral vitamin D supplements modestly worsened cardiometabolic risk factors compared with placebo in adults, raising LDL cholesterol by 0.136 mmol/L, systolic blood pressure by 2.79 mm Hg, fasting blood glucose by 0.11 mmol/L and HbA1c by 0.164%.
label: False

claim: A recent systematic review and meta-analysis of annual CO2 flux data from 120 peatland sites worldwide found that emissions rise by about 7.2 gCO2-C per square metre per year for every centimetre the water table drops, and that restored peatlands remained net CO2 sources on average.
label: True

claim: A recent systematic review and meta-analysis of annual CO2 flux data from 120 peatland sites worldwide found that emissions fall by about 7.2 gCO2-C per square metre per year for every centimetre the water table drops, and that restored peatlands had become net CO2 sinks on average.
label: False

claim: A recent global systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 studies across 33 countries found that extreme temperature is the main driver of climate change's negative impacts on arboreal mammals, with several families, particularly Pseudocheiridae, Cercopithecidae and Tarsiidae, projected to face significant future range contractions.
label: True

claim: A recent global systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 studies across 33 countries found that extreme temperature is the main driver of climate change's positive impacts on arboreal mammals, with several families, particularly Pseudocheiridae, Cercopithecidae and Tarsiidae, projected to enjoy significant future range expansions.
label: False

claim: A systematic review of 170 mouse heat-exposure studies published from 2020 to early 2025 found that 83% housed their control mice below the thermoneutral zone, while only 4% kept controls at thermoneutral temperatures, meaning heat-exposed animals are often being compared with cold-stressed controls.
label: True

claim: A systematic review of 170 mouse heat-exposure studies published from 2020 to early 2025 found that 83% housed their control mice within the thermoneutral zone, while only 4% kept controls below thermoneutral temperatures, meaning heat-exposed animals are rarely being compared with cold-stressed controls.
label: False

claim: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 studies, 7 of them pooled, on long COVID risk in people previously hospitalized for COVID-19 found that more severe acute illness or advanced respiratory support was the strongest risk factor, with about 2.5 times the odds of post-COVID outcomes (OR 2.55), while women had nearly double the odds of men (OR 1.94).
label: True

claim: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 studies, 7 of them pooled, on long COVID risk in people previously hospitalized for COVID-19 found that more severe acute illness or advanced respiratory support was the strongest protective factor, with about 2.5 times lower odds of post-COVID outcomes (OR 0.39), while women had nearly half the odds of men (OR 0.52).
label: False

claim: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of COVID-19 studies found that patients with acute high blood sugar had about twice the risk of short-term death (RR 2.09) and about 3.6 times the risk of invasive mechanical ventilation (RR 3.64). These were unadjusted associations, not proof of cause.
label: True

claim: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of COVID-19 studies found that patients with acute high blood sugar had about half the risk of short-term death (RR 0.48) and about 3.6 times lower risk of invasive mechanical ventilation (RR 0.27). These were unadjusted associations, not proof of cause.
label: False

claim: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found that adding a PCSK9 inhibitor to statin therapy after acute ischemic stroke roughly doubled the odds of functional independence (OR 2.17) and cut the odds of recurrent ischemic stroke by about two-thirds (OR 0.33), with safety comparable to statins alone, though the evidence is still preliminary.
label: True

claim: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found that adding a PCSK9 inhibitor to statin therapy after acute ischemic stroke roughly halved the odds of functional independence (OR 0.46) and tripled the odds of recurrent ischemic stroke (OR 3.03), with significantly more adverse events than statins alone, though the evidence is still preliminary.
label: False

claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of 12 mostly retrospective studies with 5,156 lung cancer patients on immune checkpoint inhibitors found that statin use was associated with a 24% lower risk of death (HR 0.76) and an 18% lower risk of disease progression (HR 0.82).
label: True

claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of 12 mostly retrospective studies with 5,156 lung cancer patients on immune checkpoint inhibitors found that statin use was associated with a 24% higher risk of death (HR 1.24) and an 18% higher risk of disease progression (HR 1.18).

claim: A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 cohort studies covering more than 126 million people found little evidence that sex changes the link between air pollution and dementia: no significant female-to-male difference for Alzheimer's disease or vascular dementia, and only a slight one for PM2.5 and overall dementia (ratio of risk ratios 1.046, 95% CI 1.024-1.069).
label: True

claim: A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 cohort studies covering more than 126 million people found that sex strongly changes the link between air pollution and dementia: women faced about four times the pollution-related risk of men for Alzheimer's disease, vascular dementia and overall dementia (ratio of risk ratios 4.6, 95% CI 4.2-5.1).
label: False
